# Dependencies {.dark-slide background-color="#111C26"}

[BLOCK 4 &middot; PART A]{.eyebrow}

::: {.accent-bar}
:::

## The five dependency fields

The `DESCRIPTION` file for each package has the following information:

| Field | Installed by default? | Attached? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Depends` | Yes | **Yes** | Needed, and attached before the package |
| `Imports` | Yes | No | Needed; used through the namespace |
| `LinkingTo` | Yes | No | Its **C/C++ headers** are needed at install time |
| `Suggests` | No | No | Used in examples, tests, vignettes, or optionally |
| `Enhances` | No | No | The package provides methods *for* it |

`install.packages()` installs `Depends`, `Imports` and `LinkingTo` by
default: the **strong** dependencies
([`?install.packages`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/install.packages.html)).

## `Depends` vs `Imports`

For `fitdistrplus`

```text
Depends: R (>= 3.5.0), MASS, grDevices, survival, methods
Imports: stats, rlang
```

`Depends` "should nowadays be used rarely", only for packages meant to be
on the user's search path. Use `Imports` for everything the package itself
needs ([R-exts](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Package-Dependencies)).

::: {.note}
[Masking]{.note-label}
`Depends` attaches the package, so it changes the user's search path. A
package that `Depends: dplyr` attaches `dplyr`, and `dplyr::filter()` then
masks `stats::filter()` in the user's session.
:::

The `R (>= x.y)` entry is what the default `R_version` filter of
`available.packages()` uses. That is why a package can be "not available"
on an older R.

## `LinkingTo`: headers at build time

```text
LinkingTo: Rcpp, BH
Imports: Rcpp
```

`LinkingTo` puts another package's headers on the compiler's include path.
It applies only to installation
([R-exts](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Package-Dependencies)).

- `LinkingTo` packages must be installed **before** the build starts.
- Upgrading `Rcpp` or `BH` changes what future builds compile against. It
  does **not** recompile packages already installed.

If you upgrade a `LinkingTo` package, reinstall the packages that link to
it.

## `Suggests` are not installed by default

Without them:

- Examples, tests and vignettes that use them cannot run
- `R CMD check` stops with an error unless told to skip them
- Optional features fail at run time with `there is no package called ...`

```r
install.packages("xml2")                          # strong only
install.packages("xml2", dependencies = TRUE)     # + Suggests of xml2
```

`dependencies = TRUE` adds `Suggests` for the packages you name, and only
strong dependencies for everything pulled in after that
([`?install.packages`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/install.packages.html)).

::: {.note}
[Site libraries]{.note-label}
Install strong dependencies, then add the specific suggested packages your
users need.
:::

## Strong vs all dependencies of `dplyr`

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

Fresh container, used until block 5:

```bash
docker run --rm -it --name rlab rocker/r-base bash
R -q
```

```r
ap <- available.packages()
tools::package_dependencies("dplyr", ap)
```

```text
$dplyr
 [1] "cli"        "generics"   "glue"       "lifecycle"  "magrittr"
 [6] "methods"    "pillar"     "R6"         "rlang"      "tibble"
[11] "tidyselect" "utils"      "vctrs"
```

```r
deps <- function(...) lengths(tools::package_dependencies("dplyr", ap, ...))
deps(recursive = TRUE)                      # strong, recursive
deps(which = "most", recursive = "strong")  # what dependencies = TRUE installs
deps(which = "most", recursive = TRUE)      # Suggests all the way down
```

```text
dplyr
   18
dplyr
   90
dplyr
 2405
```

CRAN on 2026-09-28. The numbers change daily.

## "Most dependencies"

`which = "most"` applies to `dplyr` itself. `recursive = "strong"` then
follows only `Depends`, `Imports` and `LinkingTo`
([`?package_dependencies`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/tools/html/package_dependencies.html)).
The result is:

- `dplyr`'s strong dependencies, recursively
- `dplyr`'s `Suggests`, and their strong dependencies, recursively
- not the `Suggests` of any upstream package

`install.packages(dependencies = TRUE)` installs the same set.

## `tools::package_dependencies()` arguments

```r
package_dependencies(packages = NULL, db = NULL, which = "strong",
                     recursive = FALSE, reverse = FALSE,
                     verbose = getOption("verbose"))
```

| Argument | Notes |
|---|---|
| `db` | An `available.packages()` matrix. Pass it in; the default downloads the index again. |
| `which` | `"strong"` (default), `"most"` (+ `Suggests`), `"all"` (+ `Enhances`), or field names |
| `recursive` | `TRUE`, or field names to recurse over, e.g. `"strong"` |
| `reverse` | `TRUE` gives reverse dependencies |

Source: [`?package_dependencies`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/tools/html/package_dependencies.html).

## `NULL` means not in the index

```r
tools::package_dependencies(c("R6", "notapackage"), ap)
```

```text
$R6
character(0)

$notapackage
NULL
```

`character(0)` means "found, no dependencies". `NULL` means "not in the
index"
([`?package_dependencies`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/tools/html/package_dependencies.html)).

::: {.note}
[Use it]{.note-label}
When validating a package list, `NULL` flags a package that was archived,
misspelled, or lives in a repository you have not configured.
`names(which(vapply(deps, is.null, TRUE)))` lists them.
:::

## Reverse dependencies, by type

```r
for (w in c("Depends", "Imports", "LinkingTo", "Suggests"))
  cat(sprintf("%-10s %d\n", w,
      length(tools::package_dependencies("xml2", ap, which = w,
                                         reverse = TRUE)[[1]])))
```

```text
Depends      4
Imports    473
LinkingTo    1
Suggests   213
```

The `Depends`, `Imports` and `LinkingTo` reverse dependencies need `xml2` to
install and load. The `Suggests` ones need it only for examples, tests and
optional features.

Check these inside your own library before you upgrade a package there.

## Procedure: resolve, review, impact

1. **Resolve.** Compute strong recursive dependencies of the requested list
   and record the resolved set with versions.
2. **Review.** Check licences and CRAN check pages, and look for `NULL`
   entries.
3. **Impact.** For each resolved package that is already installed, list
   the installed packages that depend on it. Test those after the upgrade.

```r
requested <- c("dplyr", "ggplot2", "xml2")
resolved  <- unique(c(requested,
  unlist(tools::package_dependencies(requested, ap, recursive = TRUE))))
length(resolved)
ap[intersect(resolved, rownames(ap)), c("Version", "NeedsCompilation")]
```

## Impact: installed packages that depend on an upgrade

Compute reverse dependencies against your library, not against CRAN
([`?package_dependencies`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/tools/html/package_dependencies.html)):

```r
inst     <- installed.packages(lib.loc = "/opt/rlibs/4.6")
upgraded <- intersect(resolved, rownames(inst))
affected <- tools::package_dependencies(upgraded, db = inst,
                                        reverse = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
sort(unique(unlist(affected)))
```

These are the packages to load and test after the upgrade.
